title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 159 (Penalty for default of certain provisions relating to DIN)

content.overview: Section 159 provides that if any individual or director of a company makes any default in complying with any of the provisions of section 152, section 155 and section 156, such individual or director of the company shall be liable to a penalty as specified in the section.
content.glance: Default under ss. 152, 155 or 156 attracts the penalty in s. 159 for the individual or director concerned.
content.study: If any individual or director of a company makes any default in complying with any of the provisions of section 152, section 155 and section 156, such individual or director of the company shall be liable to a penalty of up to the amount provided in the section (as in force). Typical breaches include acting without a DIN, obtaining more than one DIN, or failing to intimate DIN to the company. The penalty under s. 159 does not by itself automatically invalidate all corporate acts already done; validity of acts turns on the other appointment and validity sections. Current-law framing: identify the defaulting provision (152/155/156); apply s. 159 penalty to the individual or director.

sections.heading: Covered Defaults
sections.body: Defaults under section 152 (appointment formalities including DIN/consent), section 155 (more than one DIN), and section 156 (director’s intimation of DIN).

sections.heading: Who Is Liable
sections.body: The individual or director who makes the default.

sections.heading: Penalty
sections.body: Penalty as provided in the section (amount as in force for the relevant default).

sections.heading: Effect on Corporate Acts
sections.body: The penalty is a personal consequence; whether board or company acts remain valid depends on the other sections, not solely on s. 159.

provisions.title: Penalty for default of certain provisions

examples.title: Second DIN
examples.body: A person who already holds a DIN obtains another. Default under s. 155 attracts penalty under s. 159.

examples.title: No intimation
examples.body: An existing director fails to intimate the DIN to the company under s. 156. Section 159 penalty is engaged.

hypotheticals.question: Does s. 159 penalty automatically void every resolution passed while the director lacked a DIN?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 159 imposes a penalty on the individual or director. Validity of corporate acts is governed by the appointment and validity provisions, not solely by the penalty section.

distinctions.title: Penalty for DIN defaults (s. 159) vs obligation to indicate DIN (s. 158)
distinctions.right: Duty to quote DIN in relevant filings

misconceptions.trap: Section 159 covers every possible DIN-related failure including company filing under s. 157.
misconceptions.correction: Section 159 as framed targets defaults under sections 152, 155 and 156 by the individual or director. Company filing defaults under other sections have their own consequences.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 159 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify default under s. 152, 155 or 156. II. Apply penalty to individual/director. III. Note limits on automatic invalidity of acts. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Default facts; section breached; penalty claim; precise relief.

examTips: Liability is of the individual or director.
Penalty ≠ automatic voidness of all acts.
